title: Canonical pullback on affine Picard n-torsion is bijective
statement: Let $k\subseteq k\prime$ be algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension], let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a smooth connected affine curve [def-sc-curves], and let $P$ with projections $\pi:P\to C$ and $g:P\to\operatorname{Spec}k\prime$ be a pullback square for this extension. For $n\geq1$ nonzero in $k$, the canonical map $\{L\in\operatorname{Pic}(C):L^n=1\}\to\{M\in\operatorname{Pic}(P):M^n=1\}$ sending $L$ to $\pi^*L$ [def-sc-picard-group] is bijective.

source.place: Proper-case Kummer naturality sentence and affine-case Picard-torsion paragraph

proof.text: Choose a smooth proper connected compactification c. Smoothness, regularity, and connectedness make its ambient scheme integral, hence irreducible, so dimension one gives smooth relative dimension one; this property is stable under base change by the existing Mathlib instance (no appeal to curve_baseChange_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one). The boundary is nonempty: an empty boundary makes the open immersion c.i an isomorphism, making f proper and affine, contrary to dimension one by lem-sc-proper-affine-finite. Choose a point of the boundary and use the compactification closedness assertion to regard it as a closed point.

Apply pic_affine_base_change_compatibility to obtain G, Gprime, Lambda, Lambdaprime, and quotient equivalences e and eprime. Define r and s as the quotient projections followed by these equivalences; both are surjective. Restrict its Picard pullback j to a homomorphism j0:G -> Gprime. The compatibility formula says s(j0(x))=b(r(x)), where b is the canonical affine Picard pullback. The supplied boundary equivalence lifts every y in ker(s) to x in ker(r) with j0(x)=y; membership in these kernels follows from QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff.

Use picZero_torsion_base_change on c.g and the supplied subgroup models to get injectivity of j0 and lifting of n-torsion. Degree-zero divisibility of c.g supplies an nth root in G of any L in G, by its equality with c.g.picZero.

Prove the representative quotient comparison directly. For equality of image classes lift them to a,a-prime in G. The image of a/a-prime has s-value one, hence equals j0(l) for l in ker(r). Injectivity of j0 gives a/a-prime=l, and applying r gives equality of the classes. For a torsion class in B lift it to y in Gprime. Then s(y^n)=1, so lift y^n to l in ker(r). Choose z in G with z^n=l. Then (y/j0(z))^n=1, and torsion lifting gives t^n=1 and j0(t)=y/j0(z). Thus j0(z*t)=y and r(z*t)^n=r(l)=1, proving surjectivity on torsion. The private Lean lemma quotient_torsion_comparison proves both conclusions using only these homomorphism identities.

Let E=hpi.isoPullback. The torsion map induced by Pic.map E.hom has inverse induced by Pic.map E.inv; Pic.map_comp and the two isomorphism identities prove both inverse equations. Compose this bijection with the canonical affine torsion comparison. Pic.map_comp and hpi.isoPullback_hom_fst prove that the composite is exactly the subtype map of the statement.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_picard_torsion_base_change
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsAlgClosed k'] [Algebra k k']
    (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C]
    (P : Scheme.{u}) (π : P ⟶ C) (g : P ⟶ Spec (.of k'))
    (hπ : IsPullback π g f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (hn : (n : k) ≠ 0) :
    Function.Bijective (fun x : {x : C.Pic // x ^ n = 1} =>
      (⟨Scheme.Pic.map π x.1, by
        change (Scheme.Pic.mapHom π x.1) ^ n = 1
        rw [← map_pow, x.2, map_one]⟩ : {x : P.Pic // x ^ n = 1}))
